newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end up, hopes of gains next week.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end up, hopes of gains next week.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to higher Friday, with hopes that more gains will come next week on boosts to U.S. Treasuries and uplifting news on foreign acquisitions of Argentine companies.
"The market was sustained at the end. I think it could open strong Monday," as gains in U.S. Treasuries did not fully translate into the local market this session, said a trader at a local brokerage.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 93-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.10 to 116.25.

Another trader said the market's firm undertone this week was underpinned by the announcement of yet more foreign acquisitions Friday, showing that investors abroad are sufficiently confident continue with large direct investments in the country.
"These are positive signals," said the trader.

Otherwise the market was keenly awaiting the expiry of Brazil's global bond offering and Brady exchange next week and Venezuela's upcoming bond offering. The Brazil deal could be decisive in the market's performance next week, traders said.
Call money rates fell to 5.98 percent from 6.48 percent.
